hits.draft:
"Articles of impeachment introduced" does not mean someone has been impeached.

Any House member can file them. They go to committee, and most never get a vote.

Before you share the headline, look up the resolution on congress.gov and check its status and how many co-sponsors it has. That tells you if it's real momentum or just a press release.
hits.video_tip: 10s: you search congress.gov, open a resolution, zoom in on 'Referred to Committee' and the co-sponsor count. On-screen text: 'Filed ≠ impeached.'

patterns: Post-election taunt was the runaway #1: Gunther's 'Democrats, now that you have control... by February I better have gas under $2' (~1.99M, 1.0% likes), a promise-ledger framing that drew reach more than love

Lame-duck urgency earned the strongest engagement: Mike Lee 'stay in session, confirm all 135 nominees' (~510k at 8.2%) and DeSantis 'roll in cots' before Jan 3 (~323k at 4.2%); 4 nominee/session hits ~930k at 6.5%
Thune blame wave continued from election night: 11 Thune hits ~990k at 9.4% likes, with 'lost it the day Thune was put in charge' (~84k at 15.5%) and the Schumer-thanked-Thune jab (~101k at 15.9%)
Alaska same-name Senate race was the cross-account story: 5 hits ~886k (Gunther 626-vote margin ~409k, rawsalerts 'which Dan Sullivan' ~312k), high reach but only 1.3% likes
Breaking-news reach without love: rawsalerts' Hegseth impeachment articles (~566k at 1.8%); 8 Hegseth/impeachment hits ~809k at 2.4%
Keywords: Democrats, Senate, Thune, nominees, Jan 3, Alaska/Sullivan, Texas/Dan Patrick, DeSantis, Jeffries 100-day list, Hegseth, Iran
virals_narrative: Outsider AI sweep (last ~48h, three searches, ~73 posts) was thin again with no breakout. Top items: @NewsfromScience on Anthropic reporting AI cracked a decades-old cell-biology mystery (~28k), @kimmonismus on Cat Wu (Claude Code/Cowork) moving to OpenAI (~28k), @firstadopter on an OpenAI 'Dot' agent proactively sending earnings-call notes (~17k), and @alexrkonrad on Cowboy launching an AI-agent app store with $5M (~14k). Smaller threads: NVIDIA open-sourcing Auto Ontology (semantic layer for agents), South Korea's sovereign-AI budget push, Musk calling Grok Bot costs 'unsustainably high', and a physicist test of five AI agents. The single top-viewed item was crypto 'AI inference mesh' spam (~44k). On the watchlist, alx flagged Rep. Ansari calling for Democrats to 'ban artificial superintelligence' (~21k).
narrative_synthesis: Day-after window (Wed ~11:07 ET to Thu ~11:10 ET): 148 hits, 137 stars and ~10.0M views from 150 originals, volume down sharply from election night. The story moved from results to what comes next: taunting Democrats to deliver on promises (the #1 post, ~1.99M), a lame-duck push to confirm Trump's nominees before Jan 3 (the best like rates), more Thune blame, the Alaska same-name Senate race, and rawsalerts' Hegseth impeachment headline. For @patriotpunishr0, the openings are useful next-step posts: save promise receipts, read your sample ballot, call your senators during the lame duck, and know that 'impeachment articles filed' is not impeachment.
